items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to review, fix and approve pull requests
points: Claude can now review pull requests, fix problems it finds and approve routine code changes, Reuters, TechCrunch and The Verge report.
Digital Trends describes it as an expansion of Claude Code's existing review tools.
The New Stack and Superpower Daily say approvals cover routine changes and follow rules each team sets.
items.for_you: Teams using Claude Code can let Claude approve routine pull requests within rules they set, not just comment on them.

items.headline: Anthropic adds zero-data-retention option for its most advanced models
points: Anthropic now offers a zero-data-retention option for its advanced models, Engadget, Quartz and Anadolu report.
Engadget says the change loosens retention rules for using the Mythos and Fable models; Startup Fortune says enterprises can keep Claude logs in their own cloud.
The Next Web and Interesting Engineering say Anthropic can still watch for misuse without storing companies' data.
items.for_you: Enterprise customers using Anthropic's top models can ask for their data not to be retained by Anthropic.

items.headline: Google Search AI Mode can now use your Wallet, with Drive and Gemini next
points: Users can choose to connect Google Wallet, Drive and the Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode for personalized answers.
Android Authority says Wallet works now and Drive and Gemini are coming soon; MLQ.ai says Drive will follow within weeks.
Google says the connections are opt-in.
items.for_you: If you use AI Mode in Search, you can now choose to let it read your Wallet cards, with Drive files and Gemini chats to follow.

items.headline: Gemini API adds file slicing to limit what the model reads
points: Google added file slicing controls to the Gemini API, so developers can choose which parts of a large file the model processes.
MLQ.ai says developers pay only for the pages and clips the model actually reads.
Unite.AI reports native support for Office files arrived alongside it.
items.for_you: Developers sending long PDFs, videos or Office files to the Gemini API can cut token costs by sending only the parts they need.

points: Google DeepMind published work using teams of AI agents and formal verification to improve quantum algorithms.
DeepMind says the work targets algorithms for fusion and chemistry; The Next Web reports the agents found cheaper algorithms and proved them correct.

items.headline: GPT-6.2 Sol becomes available in ChatGPT's regular chat
points: OpenAI has brought GPT-6.2 Sol to ChatGPT's chat tab for paid users, MacRumors, 9to5Mac and Superpower Daily report.
The Decoder says OpenAI claims the update handles complex everyday questions, web searches and images more reliably.
9to5Mac reports OpenAI also set a retirement date for two older models.
items.for_you: Paid ChatGPT users now get GPT-6.2 Sol in ordinary chats and should check whether a model they rely on is being retired.

items.headline: California attorney general sues OpenAI over model security and public safety
points: California Attorney General Bonta has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, Reuters and PYMNTS report.
Both say the suit concerns the security of OpenAI's AI models and public safety; no court has ruled yet.

items.headline: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, an open-source Linux security runtime
points: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source runtime that protects running Linux systems while teams roll out patches.
The WSJ describes it as a project to safeguard agentic AI; SiliconANGLE says it aims to block AI-driven cyberattacks.
items.for_you: Teams running Linux servers can try Shirudo, which is open source, to protect systems while patches are still rolling out.

items.headline: OpenAI starts OpenWorks, paying local experts to coach small businesses
points: OpenAI launched OpenWorks, which pays local AI experts to coach small businesses in AI for free, MLQ.ai and Decrypt report.
Decrypt says coaches can earn up to $8,000; Superpower Daily says it starts in 20 U.S. communities, including Charleston, per Live 5 News.
items.for_you: Small businesses in participating U.S. communities can get free coaching on using AI.

items.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over sexualized images made by Grok
points: Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX, X and xAI over Grok producing sexualized images of real people, including children, AP, Reuters and the NYT report.
Anadolu says they are the first U.S. states to sue over Grok images; Virginia's attorney general also alleges false safety claims.
Several outlets say the suits target a 'spicy mode'; Tom's Guide says they cite 3 million images.
